content.comment_body: Hello, I am new to this forum and to [product_name] [version_no]. I have set up a system with a log file and want to sample data every hour. Currently, I can retrieve the logfile to my computer, but the timestamp structure is unclear. How can I make this work?
Hi [user_name], can you specify where your issue lies? Is it during DataLog creation or when analyzing the CSV file? Please share an example of your problem.
I plan to log temperature data. This week, I will install some sensors and connect a module for measuring. My goal is to monitor both the outdoor and pond temperature every hour.
It looks like your question hasn't been resolved yet. Are you having trouble with: a) creating the DataLog, or b) interpreting the DataLog results?
I've attached an example in the file.

I created a data log and have read out the data, but I want the system to log data every hour. Currently, the logging times seem random. I've attached the file. Maybe I need to set up the logging configuration differently.

Thanks [user_name] for sharing information. I modified the logfile and now receive data every minute in the CSV. I've adjusted the TH and TL parameters, but I'm not sure what the TA parameter refers to in your image.
The simulation I previously ran measures elapsed time. The DataLog runs every minute because the defined interval is set to seconds rather than minutes.
I now have a basic setup for logging. I expect the sensors to arrive tomorrow. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced difficulty configuring structured hourly data logging for temperature monitoring with [product_name] [version_no]. The primary challenge was setting up precise logging intervals, as data was logged at random times by default, resulting in unstructured records. With guidance, the user learned to adjust timing parameters and managed to record data every minute, though the configuration process was not intuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple and accessible method to set up data logging at precise hourly intervals, ensuring consistent readings. They also seek clear instructions on parameter configuration and log structure.
